SAPO's Big Ideas

By: Annalise Lubbe | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The Post Office was declared commercially insolvent yet the new CEO plans to turn this state entity into a leader in ecommerce and courier services.

Unique Selling Point:
The South African Post Office wants to become a prominent player in the country’s courier industry and ecommerce offering, despite the fact that the Auditor-General has declared it commercially insolvent. How will this struggling state-entity turn around their ‘obsolete business model’ and become financially sustainable when they are unable to pay their long line of creditors and without further bailouts from the National Treasury?

Summary:
Despite R8 billion in bailouts since 2014, the South African Post Office is once again staring bankruptcy in the face, with reports of unpaid rentals and desperate suppliers, postal backlogs and broken ICT systems.

But the recently appointed CEO, Nomkhita Mona, is optimistic: “we want to grow and build a world-class, commercially viable postal service with no heavy reliance on national fisus”, she says. Mona plans to expand into the highly lucrative e-commerce space as well as having the monopoly on being the only service provider on the market to deliver packages weighing 1kg or less.

In April the Post Office announced a strategic partnership with Wish, the largest and fastest growing global ecommerce platform connecting with more than 100 million monthly active users in over 100 countries to over 500,000 merchants around the world.

We ask how the commercially insolvent state-entity plans to compete with private courier companies to deliver a reliable service and enter the e-commerce market if it cannot even pay rent, postal agents and deliver parcels on time?


Further information:
The struggling post office has had a string of CEO’s since August 2019, following Mark Barne’s hasty departure. Acting CEO Lindiwe Kwele was suspended in December 2019 on the basis of whistle-blower allegations of conflicts of interest and the irregular extensions of contracts. Ivumile Nongogo replaced Lindiwe as acting CEO, but he stepped down after the post office board decided to institute disciplinary charges against him for concluding an agreement with the SA Social Security Agency to distribute the temporary Covid-19 R350 relief grant, without consulting the board. Reneilwe Langa, seconded from the department of communications and digital technologies, was then appointed acting CEO, and was replaced by Nomkhita Mona in March this year as the new CEO of the South African Post Office.

But will the new CEO manage to turn the negative financial position around and save the cash flow problems when it has recorded a loss of nearly R1-billion in the first quarter of 2020? The entity's financial position is so dire it now needs more than R7-billion in additional funding from the government to stay afloat but the government is currently facing a record budget deficit and has been trying to stop giving bailouts to state-owned enterprises.

The Post Office is temporarily closing 53, or about 3.7 percent, of its branches, citing payment disputes but said its revenue has increased after a difficult COVID-19 lockdown period and this will help it to address creditor backlogs. Mona says she has engaged with the creditors and plans to honour their commitment of debt.

She also expects the national government to support SAPO’s efforts in dealing with legacy issues and will still knock on the government’s door for more taxpayer funded bailouts. Her long-term plan is to build a world-class commercially viable postal service. This she aims to do by expanding into the highly lucrative ecommerce spacem, digitising its processes, the courier space as well as those activities which fall within SAPO’s legal mandate.

Creditor backlog: The people most affected by the dire finances of the Post Office are the Postal Agents spread to the furthest corners of the country providing an essential service to the poorest of the poor in both rural and urban areas. Postal Agents receive a basic salary and commission for every transaction they make. They are solely responsible for the operational cost and do not get any medical aid or pension from the post office. Postal against were put into place in 2006 to help the post office save on operational cost, medical aid and pension fund. Rental issues are the second major creditor backlog faced by SAPO. Many Post Offices have closed their doors due to unpaid rent and landlords running out of patients waiting for their rent.

Courier space: The South Africa Post Office is heading to court to block courier companies from delivering packages weighing 1kg and less. In a ruling handed down in late 2019, communications regulator Icasa found that PostNet had contravened the Postal Services Act by transporting and delivering such packages. As the only operator of its kind in South Africa, the Post Office has the exclusive right to provide delivery services for all letters, postcards, printed, matter, small parcels and other postal articles up to including 1kg. In March 2020, PostNet secured an interdict which allowed it to continue to deliver these packages until the full challenge was heard in the Gauteng High Court.

The Post Office’s belief that it could become a major courier could be based on the assumption that it will get a favourable outcome in an ongoing court matter which could send shockwaves through the industry as South Africans will be forced to use the Post Office for deliveries of any parcels below 1kg in weight, regardless of its reputation and financial standing. Worryingly, these could include important deliveries such as passports, visas and bank cards. The Post Office does not have the capital needed to upscale its logistics to compete with private courier companies, says Anton Roets, defense attorney for PostNet. Its annual results show that it has incurred financial losses of R1.76 billion, making it the 14th year in a row that the entity has not posted a profit. Its current liabilities also exceed assets by R1,49-billion, which means it is unable to pay its debts and resulted in the Auditor-General declaring it commercially insolvent. In addition, the Post Office's courier and parcel revenue declined by R187 million in 2020. This they blame on the COVID-19 pandemic preventing the company from making deliveries. In contrast, however, many courier companies - including FedEX and Aramex - have shown a positive performance due to more consumers using online shopping and relying on delivery services to get basic goods and other products.

E-commerce expansion: The Post Office has the largest retail footprint in the country. It therefore comes as no surprise that Wish, one of the largest and fastest growing global ecommerce platforms plans to tap into this existing network to gain access to the South African consumer market. In a first of its kind for SAPO entered into a partnership with Wish in April with the aim to provide a faster, high quality service to customers throughout South African Post. The process will involve end to end tracking visibility and delivery confirmation, customers to receive bundled shipments for multiple items and SMS and physical notifications on deliveries awaiting collection.

Then on the 1st of June another agreement was signed between the Post Office and Mail Americas, an eCommerce platform which specialises in cross-border business-to-customer solutions to postal operators. It focuses on connecting business with customers in Latin America and Africa. In terms of the agreement the South African Post Office will provide distribution services to clients of Mail Americas in South African and the subcontinent.

The Covid-19 pandemic has seen a shift towards eCommerce in Southern Africa and has more than doubled over the last two years, says expert, Arthurs Goldstuck who conducted a recent study to analyse the trends into this industry. The Post Office with its 1500 branches all over South Africa, says it is in the right position to give all South Africans access to eCommerce, including those outside cities. But in the latest news, the Post Office has announced that it will be closing 130 branches countrywide as part of their plan to save cost.

The story:
We interview Lezel Jacobs, a Postal Agent from Pella in Western Cape who are one of many we spoke to over the phone who have not been paid their basic salary and commission since January; we speak to attorney Nicole Swart, representing her client - a landlord - and the outstanding debt from rent owned for 5 Post Offices in the Pretoria district; we ask pertinent questions to the new CEO on how she plans to turn the state-entity around with her new plans and honour the outstanding debt to creditors; we speak to Anton Roets, attorney for Postnet about the looming court case brought about by the Post Office and ICASA against the courier company and the South African Express Parcel Association (SAEPA) about the 1kg category which the Post Office is laying claim to; we get an expert on board, Arthur Goldstuck, to speak about the fast growing e-commerce space and why the Post Office intends to expand into this highly lucrative space as part of their strategic planning to get back on their feet.

Return flight: Producer to Gauteng; accommodation x 1 night; car rental x 2 days

Script:


Script: SAPO’S big ideas
Date: 30 July 2021
Duration: 10.6 seconds

Link: Many of us grew up with the post office as part of an institution, our very first savings book, buying postage stamps, paying municipal bills and vehicle licenses, but with the move to the digital world, it was left behind.

V/O As businesses digitize, relying on email and smartphone apps, the South African Post Office has become virtually obsolete - a relic from byone era. Add poor service delivery to the mix and you have a disaster waiting to happen. In 2018 the South African Post Office received a bail out of R2.947 billion from the government due to mismanagement and overspending and in March the state entity was declared commercially insolvent by the Auditor General, Tsakani Maluleke. A new CEO at the helm has big plans to improve the service - but can she deliver?

Nomkhita Mona: Group CEO South African Post Office - People ask me why take on this huge challenge. It is because I see the challenge but I equally see the opportunity. And in my eyes they outweigh the challenges.

Derek Watts: Now the auditor general says you are commercially insolvent. What are the contributing factors?

Nomkhita Mona: ​As a newly appointed CEO three months ago I wanted to know that as well and we went back 5,6 years ago this is when this ship actually went down. This is not an overnight failure.

Derek Watts: Now the auditor general’s report says SAPO is at a critical juncture and if the entity is not restructured and repurposed it will collapse.

Nomkhita Mona: Hundred percent. I agree with that. We do need to change everything about the Post Office. We need to modernise. We do need to restructure.We cannot do things in the same way as we did them 20,30, 50 years ago.

V/O Restructuring includes cost cutting. In May the Post Office announced the closure of branches in a short radius in urban areas, across the country, to boost revenue.

Link: This branch of the post office in ElardusPark in Pretoria recently closed its doors indefinitely, just one of 130 branches targeted for closure.

Nomkhita Mona: So that is where our focus is right now. Cost cutting, cost containment but bring in those new revenue lines.


V/O While businesses have floundered during the pandemic, Information and Communication Technology analyst Arthur Goldstuck says that lockdowns and restrictions have created an environment for e-commerce to flourish.

Arthur Goldstuck: Digital analyst - The pandemic has been a massive catalyst. The total of online retail in sa in 2020 was just over 30 billion rand which made up about 3% of total retail in sa. that is expected to increase in 2021 to around R42 billion. So you are talking about jumping to around 4% of total retail, and then the following year going up to about R50 billion rand so 5%.

V/O And eyeing a slice of the e-pie the Post Office has entered into partnerships with two of the largest global e-commerce platforms, Wish and MailAmericas, to handle the distribution of parcels for the retail giants.

Derek Watts: What revenue do you expect to earn from this partnership?

Nomkhita Mona: A regulated price that we charge per parcel that we handle. So those kind of fees can go into hundred of millions. Already we are sitting at 200 just on those Wish.com and MailAmericas and they themselves are calling us and say we would like to work with you.

Arthur Goldstuck: The industry that truly exploded during the pandemic was the courier industry. From the individual with a car through to the big courier companies with massive demand from e-commerce, we saw an explosion at all levels.

V/O Online retail goes hand in hand with courier services, a booming industry. The Post Office says they should have exclusive rights to the small parcel courier market.

Link: In a pending court case the Post office is trying to block courier companies like PostNet from delivering parcels weighing less than 1Kg, leaving your precious package in their hands.

V/O In 2017 the South African Post Office filed a complaint against PostNet saying the Post Office has a statutory monopoly to deliver articles of less than a kilogram. In a ruling handed down in late 2019, communications regulator ICASA found that PostNet had contravened the Postal Services Act and had to cease couriering these articles. In March 2020 PostNet secured an interdict which allowed it to continue until the case is finally determined in the Gauteng High Court. Supporting PostNet in this case is the South Afrian Express Parcel Association with its 100-strong membership. Anton Roets is the legal representative for PostNet.

Anton Roets; Attorney for PostNet - So what you have on the one hand, you have the post office arguing that that act gives them a statutory monopoly over the couriering of articles less than a kilogram. We have a different take on it. We say when you read the act properly interpreted, what the act does, it gives the post office a statutory monopoly over postal services not courier services. We feel quite strongly that our interpretation is correct on the wording of the act but we also believe that when you look at certain constitutional rights that also supports our position.

Nomkhita Mona: We are basically saying by law in SA only the Post Office has the mandate to distribute any parcels between zero and one kilogram. Remember why this law was put together. It is to make sure that we are being helped as sa post office to subsidise those who we will never be able to make money on so it is about how we serve the communities.

V/O Should the Post Office win the case it will remove the choice for online business owners like Pinni Goodman who sell mainly small items all weighing less than 1Kg.

Derek Watts: Are you very worried about this pending decision, are you having sleepless nights?

Pinni Goodman: Online retailer - I wouldn’t say sleepless nights but I would say it is quite a worry for us if we had to adjust to that. We would have to make a lot of modifications, we would never be able to offer the same sort of service that we currently offer which for us is huge, it is all in the service for us. If you look at our reviews, it is all fast delivery, fast delivery; i ordered this morning, i got it today, i got it tomorrow. That is what it is all about. E-commerce is all about that.

V/O It will be a mammoth task for the Post Office to win back the public’s trust that it can deliver. At the end of December 2020 the Post Office owed creditors R2.54 billion according to the National Treasury. Perhaps the most desperate situation is with the Postal Agents.There are 2058 agents spread across the country to perform a basic service to handle mail on behalf of the Post Office for which they are paid a stipend and small commission on all registered mail. Lezel Jacobs from Pela - a village on the outskirts of Atlantis on the Cape west coast - is one of them.

Lezel Jacobs: Postal Agent - Ek is nou vyf jaar n posagent (I have been a Postal Agent for five years,) en ek was baie lief vir my werk (and I love my work), ek is nog steeds lief vir my werk (I still love my work,) maar nou op die oomblik gaan dinge nie so lekker nie. (but at present things aren’t going well.).

V/OPostal agents pay their own rent, electricity, and buy their own consumables. In Jacobs’s case, she was lucky enough to get this room from the church rent-free but electricity is not included.

Lezel Jacobs: Huidiglik moet ek my eie krag koop (Presently, I buy my own electricity,), en dan het ek n probleem met my poskantoor se dak, dit lek, (and then I have a problem with my post office’s roof, it leaks.) Dis nou winter en 3, 4 weke gelede toe was daar in inbraak in my poskantoor. (It is now winter and three, four weeks ago there was a burglary in my post office.). Hulle het my dagstemp gevat, (They took my stamp) hulle het al my penne, al my stationary gevat, en my krag. (...they took all my pens, all my stationery, and my power.)

Up sound: Hoe gaan dit? Pietie, luister die water briewe het nog nie gekom nie.

Lezel Jacobs: Toe die lockdown begin het in april (When lockdown started in April,) toe was ons betaal in April gewees en toe eers weer in oktober (I was paid and then only again in October….) die 20ste oktober, en toe na oktober die 9de february.(...and then after October, the 9th of February.) Wie kan so aangaan? (Who can carry on like that?)

Derek Watts: Postal agents around the country say they have not been paid for months, going right back to February this year.

Nomkhita Mona: It is correct yah. Some of them have reached out to my office that we haven’t been able to pay because the financial situation of the post office is really a bit bad right now but we are working on it.

Derek Watts: When can they expect payment?

Nomkhita Mona: We are very careful not to give a date because we really don't know. If that date comes and we are not able to pay, then we can’t give our word but the important thing is to keep them informed.

Derek Watts: Nomkhita, where do you get money to pay the landlords, pay the postal agents, and get SAPO back on its feet?

Nomkita Mona: We have a number of initiatives that we are putting together; some of them are coming from the e-commerce side. We are looking at partnerships to actually even go cashless. So it is the e-commerce; it's the digitisation, it's the modernisation of the post office.

V/O And for the new leader, partnership is what it's all about. In a recent development the Post Office has sent out a ‘request for interest’, inviting private courier companies to come on board and work with the Post Office in the 1kg reserved market. While the Post Office has big ideas for the future, it means little for the postal agents like Jacobs who are expected to wait patiently for payment.

Lezel Jacobs: Ja ek voel hartseer. (Yes, I feel sad.) Ons agente, hulle dink niks van ons nie (Us agents, they think nothing of us.) En ons doen onse bes om die poskantoortjies hier op die kleinhoewe oop te hou (And we are doing our best to keep our little post offices open here in the small holdings, )maar hulle sit daarbo in kantore en verwag die werk moet gedoen word (but they sit in their offices and expect the work must be done) maar dan betaal hulle nie vir ons nie. (but then they don't pay us.) Hulle dink niks van ons nie. (They think nothing of us.)

Derek Watts: Nomkhita I think South Africans citizens have become cynical about government agencies with them being efficient and even profitable.

Nomkhita Mona: Understandably so. Because we have not come out smelling like roses as government agencies on many, many areas and I suppose which is why they come to people like us now and say come and help run this business and see if you can’t turn it around.

________________________________________________________________________

Promo one - 21 seconds:
V/O With long queues and late deliveries, the South African Post Office has long been perceived as inefficient - a relic from byone era. A new CEO at the helm says she has big plans to improve the service - but can she deliver?
Up sound: Nomkhita Mona: I see the challenge but I equally see the opportunity. And in my eyes they outweigh the challenges.

Promo two - 21 seconds:
V/O As the fourth industrial revolution demands communication and e-commerce at the speed of light and in cyberspace - what’s to become of the South African Post Office? Will it even have a place in this new world?
Up sound: Nomkhita Mona: The important thing about what happens to a company is you need to get the right leader at the right phase. I believe I am the right leader at this phase.

Promo three - 11 seconds:
The new CEO says the South African Post Office is back with a bang but what does it mean for consumers who have long lost their trust in this failed dinosaur of a bygone era.

nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 19 August 2021 Script: Script: SAPO’S big ideas Date: 30 July 2021 Duration: 10.6 seconds Link: Many of us grew up with the post office as part of an institution, our very first savings book, buying postage stamps, paying municipal bills and vehicle licenses, but with the move to the digital world, it was left behind. V/O As businesses digitize, relying on email and smartphone apps, the South African Post Office has become virtually obsolete - a relic from byone era. Add poor service delivery to the mix and you have a disaster waiting to happen. In 2018 the South African Post Office received a bail out of R2.947 billion from the government due to mismanagement and overspending and in March the state entity was declared commercially insolvent by the Auditor General, Tsakani Maluleke. A new CEO at the helm has big plans to improve the service - but can she deliver? Nomkhita Mona: Group CEO South African Post Office - People ask me why take on this huge challenge. It is because I see the challenge but I equally see the opportunity. And in my eyes they outweigh the challenges. Derek Watts: Now the auditor general says you are commercially insolvent. What are the contributing factors? Nomkhita Mona: ​As a newly appointed CEO three months ago I wanted to know that as well and we went back 5,6 years ago this is when this ship actually went down. This is not an overnight failure. Derek Watts: Now the auditor general’s report says SAPO is at a critical juncture and if the entity is not restructured and repurposed it will collapse. Nomkhita Mona: Hundred percent. I agree with that. We do need to change everything about the Post Office. We need to modernise. We do need to restructure.We cannot do things in the same way as we did them 20,30, 50 years ago. V/O Restructuring includes cost cutting. In May the Post Office announced the closure of branches in a short radius in urban areas, across the country, to boost revenue. Link: This branch of the post office in ElardusPark in Pretoria recently closed its doors indefinitely, just one of 130 branches targeted for closure. Nomkhita Mona: So that is where our focus is right now. Cost cutting, cost containment but bring in those new revenue lines. V/O While businesses have floundered during the pandemic, Information and Communication Technology analyst Arthur Goldstuck says that lockdowns and restrictions have created an environment for e-commerce to flourish. Arthur Goldstuck: Digital analyst - The pandemic has been a massive catalyst. The total of online retail in sa in 2020 was just over 30 billion rand which made up about 3% of total retail in sa. that is expected to increase in 2021 to around R42 billion. So you are talking about jumping to around 4% of total retail, and then the following year going up to about R50 billion rand so 5%. V/O And eyeing a slice of the e-pie the Post Office has entered into partnerships with two of the largest global e-commerce platforms, Wish and MailAmericas, to handle the distribution of parcels for the retail giants. Derek Watts: What revenue do you expect to earn from this partnership? Nomkhita Mona: A regulated price that we charge per parcel that we handle. So those kind of fees can go into hundred of millions. Already we are sitting at 200 just on those Wish.com and MailAmericas and they themselves are calling us and say we would like to work with you. Arthur Goldstuck: The industry that truly exploded during the pandemic was the courier industry. From the individual with a car through to the big courier companies with massive demand from e-commerce, we saw an explosion at all levels. V/O Online retail goes hand in hand with courier services, a booming industry. The Post Office says they should have exclusive rights to the small parcel courier market. Link: In a pending court case the Post office is trying to block courier companies like PostNet from delivering parcels weighing less than 1Kg, leaving your precious package in their hands. V/O In 2017 the South African Post Office filed a complaint against PostNet saying the Post Office has a statutory monopoly to deliver articles of less than a kilogram. In a ruling handed down in late 2019, communications regulator ICASA found that PostNet had contravened the Postal Services Act and had to cease couriering these articles. In March 2020 PostNet secured an interdict which allowed it to continue until the case is finally determined in the Gauteng High Court. Supporting PostNet in this case is the South Afrian Express Parcel Association with its 100-strong membership. Anton Roets is the legal representative for PostNet. Anton Roets; Attorney for PostNet - So what you have on the one hand, you have the post office arguing that that act gives them a statutory monopoly over the couriering of articles less than a kilogram. We have a different take on it. We say when you read the act properly interpreted, what the act does, it gives the post office a statutory monopoly over postal services not courier services. We feel quite strongly that our interpretation is correct on the wording of the act but we also believe that when you look at certain constitutional rights that also supports our position. Nomkhita Mona: We are basically saying by law in SA only the Post Office has the mandate to distribute any parcels between zero and one kilogram. Remember why this law was put together. It is to make sure that we are being helped as sa post office to subsidise those who we will never be able to make money on so it is about how we serve the communities. V/O Should the Post Office win the case it will remove the choice for online business owners like Pinni Goodman who sell mainly small items all weighing less than 1Kg. Derek Watts: Are you very worried about this pending decision, are you having sleepless nights? Pinni Goodman: Online retailer - I wouldn’t say sleepless nights but I would say it is quite a worry for us if we had to adjust to that. We would have to make a lot of modifications, we would never be able to offer the same sort of service that we currently offer which for us is huge, it is all in the service for us. If you look at our reviews, it is all fast delivery, fast delivery; i ordered this morning, i got it today, i got it tomorrow. That is what it is all about. E-commerce is all about that. V/O It will be a mammoth task for the Post Office to win back the public’s trust that it can deliver. At the end of December 2020 the Post Office owed creditors R2.54 billion according to the National Treasury. Perhaps the most desperate situation is with the Postal Agents.There are 2058 agents spread across the country to perform a basic service to handle mail on behalf of the Post Office for which they are paid a stipend and small commission on all registered mail. Lezel Jacobs from Pela - a village on the outskirts of Atlantis on the Cape west coast - is one of them. Lezel Jacobs: Postal Agent - Ek is nou vyf jaar n posagent (I have been a Postal Agent for five years,) en ek was baie lief vir my werk (and I love my work), ek is nog steeds lief vir my werk (I still love my work,) maar nou op die oomblik gaan dinge nie so lekker nie. (but at present things aren’t going well.). V/OPostal agents pay their own rent, electricity, and buy their own consumables. In Jacobs’s case, she was lucky enough to get this room from the church rent-free but electricity is not included. Lezel Jacobs: Huidiglik moet ek my eie krag koop (Presently, I buy my own electricity,), en dan het ek n probleem met my poskantoor se dak, dit lek, (and then I have a problem with my post office’s roof, it leaks.) Dis nou winter en 3, 4 weke gelede toe was daar in inbraak in my poskantoor. (It is now winter and three, four weeks ago there was a burglary in my post office.). Hulle het my dagstemp gevat, (They took my stamp) hulle het al my penne, al my stationary gevat, en my krag. (...they took all my pens, all my stationery, and my power.) Up sound: Hoe gaan dit? Pietie, luister die water briewe het nog nie gekom nie. Lezel Jacobs: Toe die lockdown begin het in april (When lockdown started in April,) toe was ons betaal in April gewees en toe eers weer in oktober (I was paid and then only again in October….) die 20ste oktober, en toe na oktober die 9de february.(...and then after October, the 9th of February.) Wie kan so aangaan? (Who can carry on like that?) Derek Watts: Postal agents around the country say they have not been paid for months, going right back to February this year. Nomkhita Mona: It is correct yah. Some of them have reached out to my office that we haven’t been able to pay because the financial situation of the post office is really a bit bad right now but we are working on it. Derek Watts: When can they expect payment? Nomkhita Mona: We are very careful not to give a date because we really don't know. If that date comes and we are not able to pay, then we can’t give our word but the important thing is to keep them informed. Derek Watts: Nomkhita, where do you get money to pay the landlords, pay the postal agents, and get SAPO back on its feet? Nomkita Mona: We have a number of initiatives that we are putting together; some of them are coming from the e-commerce side. We are looking at partnerships to actually even go cashless. So it is the e-commerce; it's the digitisation, it's the modernisation of the post office. V/O And for the new leader, partnership is what it's all about. In a recent development the Post Office has sent out a ‘request for interest’, inviting private courier companies to come on board and work with the Post Office in the 1kg reserved market. While the Post Office has big ideas for the future, it means little for the postal agents like Jacobs who are expected to wait patiently for payment. Lezel Jacobs: Ja ek voel hartseer. (Yes, I feel sad.) Ons agente, hulle dink niks van ons nie (Us agents, they think nothing of us.) En ons doen onse bes om die poskantoortjies hier op die kleinhoewe oop te hou (And we are doing our best to keep our little post offices open here in the small holdings, )maar hulle sit daarbo in kantore en verwag die werk moet gedoen word (but they sit in their offices and expect the work must be done) maar dan betaal hulle nie vir ons nie. (but then they don't pay us.) Hulle dink niks van ons nie. (They think nothing of us.) Derek Watts: Nomkhita I think South Africans citizens have become cynical about government agencies with them being efficient and even profitable. Nomkhita Mona: Understandably so. Because we have not come out smelling like roses as government agencies on many, many areas and I suppose which is why they come to people like us now and say come and help run this business and see if you can’t turn it around. ________________________________________________________________________ Promo one - 21 seconds: V/O With long queues and late deliveries, the South African Post Office has long been perceived as inefficient - a relic from byone era. A new CEO at the helm says she has big plans to improve the service - but can she deliver? Up sound: Nomkhita Mona: I see the challenge but I equally see the opportunity. And in my eyes they outweigh the challenges. Promo two - 21 seconds: V/O As the fourth industrial revolution demands communication and e-commerce at the speed of light and in cyberspace - what’s to become of the South African Post Office? Will it even have a place in this new world? Up sound: Nomkhita Mona: The important thing about what happens to a company is you need to get the right leader at the right phase. I believe I am the right leader at this phase. Promo three - 11 seconds: The new CEO says the South African Post Office is back with a bang but what does it mean for consumers who have long lost their trust in this failed dinosaur of a bygone era. ___________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Invoicing Back references from Insert ID in Invoice: Title Author Last Updated Invoice for SAPO's Big Ideas (5923) Annalise Lubbe 02 August 2021

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The Post Office was declared commercially insolvent yet the new CEO plans to turn this state entity into a leader in ecommerce and courier services.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The South African Post Office wants to become a prominent player in the country’s courier industry and ecommerce offering, despite the fact that the Auditor-General has declared it commercially insolvent. How will this struggling state-entity turn around their ‘obsolete business model’ and become financially sustainable when they are unable to pay their long line of creditors and without further bailouts from the National Treasury?
metadata.Summary: Despite R8 billion in bailouts since 2014, the South African Post Office is once again staring bankruptcy in the face, with reports of unpaid rentals and desperate suppliers, postal backlogs and broken ICT systems. But the recently appointed CEO, Nomkhita Mona, is optimistic: “we want to grow and build a world-class, commercially viable postal service with no heavy reliance on national fisus”, she says. Mona plans to expand into the highly lucrative e-commerce space as well as having the monopoly on being the only service provider on the market to deliver packages weighing 1kg or less. In April the Post Office announced a strategic partnership with Wish, the largest and fastest growing global ecommerce platform connecting with more than 100 million monthly active users in over 100 countries to over 500,000 merchants around the world. We ask how the commercially insolvent state-entity plans to compete with private courier companies to deliver a reliable service and enter the e-commerce market if it cannot even pay rent, postal agents and deliver parcels on time?
metadata.Further information: The struggling post office has had a string of CEO’s since August 2019, following Mark Barne’s hasty departure. Acting CEO Lindiwe Kwele was suspended in December 2019 on the basis of whistle-blower allegations of conflicts of interest and the irregular extensions of contracts. Ivumile Nongogo replaced Lindiwe as acting CEO, but he stepped down after the post office board decided to institute disciplinary charges against him for concluding an agreement with the SA Social Security Agency to distribute the temporary Covid-19 R350 relief grant, without consulting the board. Reneilwe Langa, seconded from the department of communications and digital technologies, was then appointed acting CEO, and was replaced by Nomkhita Mona in March this year as the new CEO of the South African Post Office. But will the new CEO manage to turn the negative financial position around and save the cash flow problems when it has recorded a loss of nearly R1-billion in the first quarter of 2020? The entity's financial position is so dire it now needs more than R7-billion in additional funding from the government to stay afloat but the government is currently facing a record budget deficit and has been trying to stop giving bailouts to state-owned enterprises. The Post Office is temporarily closing 53, or about 3.7 percent, of its branches, citing payment disputes but said its revenue has increased after a difficult COVID-19 lockdown period and this will help it to address creditor backlogs. Mona says she has engaged with the creditors and plans to honour their commitment of debt. She also expects the national government to support SAPO’s efforts in dealing with legacy issues and will still knock on the government’s door for more taxpayer funded bailouts. Her long-term plan is to build a world-class commercially viable postal service. This she aims to do by expanding into the highly lucrative ecommerce spacem, digitising its processes, the courier space as well as those activities which fall within SAPO’s legal mandate. Creditor backlog: The people most affected by the dire finances of the Post Office are the Postal Agents spread to the furthest corners of the country providing an essential service to the poorest of the poor in both rural and urban areas. Postal Agents receive a basic salary and commission for every transaction they make. They are solely responsible for the operational cost and do not get any medical aid or pension from the post office. Postal against were put into place in 2006 to help the post office save on operational cost, medical aid and pension fund. Rental issues are the second major creditor backlog faced by SAPO. Many Post Offices have closed their doors due to unpaid rent and landlords running out of patients waiting for their rent. Courier space: The South Africa Post Office is heading to court to block courier companies from delivering packages weighing 1kg and less. In a ruling handed down in late 2019, communications regulator Icasa found that PostNet had contravened the Postal Services Act by transporting and delivering such packages. As the only operator of its kind in South Africa, the Post Office has the exclusive right to provide delivery services for all letters, postcards, printed, matter, small parcels and other postal articles up to including 1kg. In March 2020, PostNet secured an interdict which allowed it to continue to deliver these packages until the full challenge was heard in the Gauteng High Court. The Post Office’s belief that it could become a major courier could be based on the assumption that it will get a favourable outcome in an ongoing court matter which could send shockwaves through the industry as South Africans will be forced to use the Post Office for deliveries of any parcels below 1kg in weight, regardless of its reputation and financial standing. Worryingly, these could include important deliveries such as passports, visas and bank cards. The Post Office does not have the capital needed to upscale its logistics to compete with private courier companies, says Anton Roets, defense attorney for PostNet. Its annual results show that it has incurred financial losses of R1.76 billion, making it the 14th year in a row that the entity has not posted a profit. Its current liabilities also exceed assets by R1,49-billion, which means it is unable to pay its debts and resulted in the Auditor-General declaring it commercially insolvent. In addition, the Post Office's courier and parcel revenue declined by R187 million in 2020. This they blame on the COVID-19 pandemic preventing the company from making deliveries. In contrast, however, many courier companies - including FedEX and Aramex - have shown a positive performance due to more consumers using online shopping and relying on delivery services to get basic goods and other products. E-commerce expansion: The Post Office has the largest retail footprint in the country. It therefore comes as no surprise that Wish, one of the largest and fastest growing global ecommerce platforms plans to tap into this existing network to gain access to the South African consumer market. In a first of its kind for SAPO entered into a partnership with Wish in April with the aim to provide a faster, high quality service to customers throughout South African Post. The process will involve end to end tracking visibility and delivery confirmation, customers to receive bundled shipments for multiple items and SMS and physical notifications on deliveries awaiting collection. Then on the 1st of June another agreement was signed between the Post Office and Mail Americas, an eCommerce platform which specialises in cross-border business-to-customer solutions to postal operators. It focuses on connecting business with customers in Latin America and Africa. In terms of the agreement the South African Post Office will provide distribution services to clients of Mail Americas in South African and the subcontinent. The Covid-19 pandemic has seen a shift towards eCommerce in Southern Africa and has more than doubled over the last two years, says expert, Arthurs Goldstuck who conducted a recent study to analyse the trends into this industry. The Post Office with its 1500 branches all over South Africa, says it is in the right position to give all South Africans access to eCommerce, including those outside cities. But in the latest news, the Post Office has announced that it will be closing 130 branches countrywide as part of their plan to save cost. The story: We interview Lezel Jacobs, a Postal Agent from Pella in Western Cape who are one of many we spoke to over the phone who have not been paid their basic salary and commission since January; we speak to attorney Nicole Swart, representing her client - a landlord - and the outstanding debt from rent owned for 5 Post Offices in the Pretoria district; we ask pertinent questions to the new CEO on how she plans to turn the state-entity around with her new plans and honour the outstanding debt to creditors; we speak to Anton Roets, attorney for Postnet about the looming court case brought about by the Post Office and ICASA against the courier company and the South African Express Parcel Association (SAEPA) about the 1kg category which the Post Office is laying claim to; we get an expert on board, Arthur Goldstuck, to speak about the fast growing e-commerce space and why the Post Office intends to expand into this highly lucrative space as part of their strategic planning to get back on their feet.
